question:
Rectify the sentence by selecting the correct spelling from the options.

After the storm passed, the sun emarged from behind the clouds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. emerged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The misspelt word "emarged" should be "emerged". "Emerge" means to come out or appear from behind/within something; its past tense is "emerged". (उभरना / बाहर निकलना)

◦ Correct: After the storm passed, the sun emerged from behind the clouds.

• Spelling key: E + MERGE + D.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options — "emergad", "amergad" and "amarged" — are all incorrect spellings of the same word.

NOTE

• Related forms: emerge (verb), emergence (noun), emergent (adjective). Do not confuse "emerge" (to come out) with "merge" (to combine).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The assignment was _________ early in the morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. due.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Due" means expected or required to be finished/submitted at a particular time. An assignment that must be handed in early in the morning is "due" then. (नियत / देय)

◦ Correct: The assignment was due early in the morning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "do" is a verb (to perform an action); "doe" is a female deer; "dew" is the tiny water droplets that form on grass in the morning. None fits the sense of a deadline.

NOTE

• "due" (homophone of "dew") — remember "due date" = the date by which something must be completed or paid.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The way Sonam performs live on stage can be called the _________ one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. most perfect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" before the blank and the sense of singling out one performance above all others call for the superlative degree — "most perfect".

◦ Correct: The way Sonam performs live on stage can be called the most perfect one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "more perfect" is a comparative (used with "than"), not a superlative.

• "perfectable" is not a standard word (the correct form is "perfectible"), and "mostly perfect" ("almost entirely") changes the meaning.

NOTE

• Although "perfect" is often treated as an absolute adjective, in graded usage the superlative is formed with "the most perfect". Superlatives take "the": the most perfect, the best, the finest.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word:

Grapple
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Release.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Grapple" means to seize, grip or struggle with (hold on tightly). Its antonym is "release", meaning to let go / set free. (पकड़ना का विलोम — छोड़ देना)

◦ Example: The wrestler grappled with his opponent, then released his grip.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Wrestle" and Option 3 "Clasp" are synonyms of grapple (to grip/struggle).

• Option 2 "Grumble" (to complain) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of grapple: grip, seize, clutch, wrestle, tackle. Antonyms: release, let go, free, loosen.

question:
Select the meaningful and correctly spelt word from the given options to fill in the blank.

The oceans cover more than 70% of the Earth's surface, making them the largest _______________ on the planet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. habitat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "habitat" is the natural home or environment of animals, plants or other organisms. The oceans, being home to countless species, are the largest habitat on the planet. (आवास / प्राकृतिक वास स्थान)

◦ Correct: ... making them the largest habitat on the planet.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "hybrid" (a cross of two different things), "habitude" (a customary way of behaving) and "habit" (a regular practice) do not fit the sense of a living environment.

NOTE

• Related terms: habitat (living place), ecosystem (community of organisms + environment), biome (large ecological zone). Marine habitats include oceans, coral reefs and estuaries.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Lieutanant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lieutanant" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Lieutenant", meaning an officer ranking just below a captain (a deputy). (उपसेनानायक / लेफ्टिनेंट)

◦ Spelling key: LIEU + TEN + ANT.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Bureaucracy" (a system of government by officials), "Rendezvous" (a meeting at an agreed place/time) and "Augment" (to increase) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt words to remember: lieutenant, bureaucracy, rendezvous, entrepreneur, questionnaire, maintenance, privilege.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

He is a complete novice when it comes to driving a car.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Amateur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "novice" is a person who is new to and inexperienced in an activity; a beginner. Its closest synonym is "amateur" (a non-professional / inexperienced person). (नौसिखिया)

◦ Example: As a novice/amateur driver, he was still learning the basics.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Expert" is an antonym (a skilled, experienced person).

• Option 2 "Zealous" (very enthusiastic) and Option 4 "Swindler" (a cheat) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of novice: beginner, amateur, learner, apprentice, tyro. Antonyms: expert, professional, veteran, master.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.

Don't fight over such a trivial issue.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Insignificant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Trivial" means of little value or importance; minor. Its closest synonym is "insignificant" (unimportant). (तुच्छ / महत्वहीन)

◦ Example: They quarrelled over a trivial/insignificant matter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Complex" (complicated) and Option 4 "Tricky" (difficult) are near-opposites in sense here.

• Option 2 "Controversial" (causing disagreement) does not match "unimportant".

NOTE

• Synonyms of trivial: insignificant, petty, minor, negligible, unimportant. Antonyms: significant, important, crucial, major.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

The pineapple dessert was so delicious that we couldn't help eat it.
option_1: so delicious that we couldn't helping eat it
option_2: so that delicious we couldn't help eating it
option_4: so delicious that we couldn't help eating it
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. so delicious that we couldn't help eating it.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The expression "can't help + V-ing (gerund)" means to be unable to stop or resist doing something. So it must be "couldn't help eating it", not "couldn't help eat it".

◦ Correct: The pineapple dessert was so delicious that we couldn't help eating it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly uses "helping eat"; Option 2 wrongly places "so that delicious"; Option 3 "No substitution" keeps the error ("help eat").

• The structure "so + adjective + that" (so delicious that ...) is correct.

NOTE

• After "can't/couldn't help", always use the -ing form: "I couldn't help laughing", "She can't help worrying".

question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct.

Smart watches are the last gadgets used by younger generations.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the latest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The context is about the most recent / newest gadgets, so "the latest" is required. "latest" means most recent, while "last" means final. The definite article "the" is needed before a superlative.

◦ Correct: Smart watches are the latest gadgets used by younger generations.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "latest" (without "the") is grammatically incomplete here; "later" and "the later" mean "at a subsequent time" (comparative), which does not fit "newest".

NOTE

• "last" = final / previous (the last chapter); "latest" = most recent / newest (the latest news, the latest model).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Straight from the horse's mouth
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Directly from the person involved.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "straight from the horse's mouth" means from the original, authentic and most reliable source; directly from the person concerned. (सीधे संबंधित व्यक्ति से / विश्वसनीय स्रोत से)

◦ Example: I heard about the promotion straight from the horse's mouth — the manager told me himself.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options are literal or irrelevant interpretations that do not capture the idiomatic meaning of getting information from a reliable, first-hand source.

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "from the horse's mouth", "first-hand information", "get it from source". Antonym idea: "hearsay" or "grapevine" (unverified rumours).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My sister performed / brilliant / in the competition / yesterday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. brilliant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word describes how she performed, so it modifies the verb "performed" and must be an adverb, not the adjective "brilliant". The correct form is "brilliantly".

◦ Correct: My sister performed brilliantly in the competition yesterday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "my sister performed", "in the competition" and "yesterday" are all grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Adjectives modify nouns (a brilliant performance); adverbs modify verbs (performed brilliantly). Most adverbs of manner are formed by adding "-ly" to the adjective.

question:
Select the option that corrects the Phrasal Verb (appearing in bold letters) in the given sentence.

The burglars broke off my neighbour's house when they were away.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. broke into.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Break into" means to enter a building/place forcibly and illegally. Since burglars forcibly entered the house, the correct phrasal verb is "broke into". (जबरन घुसना / सेंध लगाना)

◦ Correct: The burglars broke into my neighbour's house when they were away.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "break off" = to stop/discontinue suddenly; "break down" = to stop functioning / to collapse emotionally; "break away" = to escape/separate from a group; "break with" = to end a relationship or tradition. None fits forced entry.

NOTE

• Useful "break" phrasal verbs: break into (enter forcibly), break out (escape / begin suddenly), break up (end a relationship), break in (enter forcibly / interrupt).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word.

They want to bifurcate the states.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Combine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bifurcate" means to divide or split something into two branches or parts. Its antonym is "combine" (to join/unite into one). (विभाजित करना का विलोम — मिलाना/जोड़ना)

◦ Example: The road bifurcates ahead, but here the two lanes combine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Divide" is a synonym of bifurcate.

• Options 3 "Examine" and 4 "Support" are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of bifurcate: divide, split, fork, separate. Antonyms: combine, unite, merge, join.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

My brother plays the guitar _________ than I do.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. better.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" signals a comparison between two people, so the comparative degree is required. The comparative of the adverb "well" is "better".

◦ Correct: My brother plays the guitar better than I do.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "best" is a superlative (used with "the", for three or more); "good" is an adjective (not an adverb of manner); "well" is the positive degree and cannot take "than".

NOTE

• Degrees of "well": well – better – best. Use "better than" for two; "the best" (with the) for three or more.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Whenever she is coming / here, she brings / many gifts for everyone.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Whenever she is coming.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Whenever" introduces a habitual/repeated action, which requires the simple present tense, not the present continuous. So it should be "Whenever she comes", not "Whenever she is coming".

◦ Correct: Whenever she comes here, she brings many gifts for everyone.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "here, she brings" and "many gifts for everyone" are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• The simple present is used for habits, routines and general truths (whenever, always, usually, every day). The present continuous is for actions happening now or temporarily.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Ravi said that / his red jacket is / the cheaper than all other jackets.
option_3: the cheaper than all other jackets.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the cheaper than all other jackets.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When comparing one item with "all other" items using "than", the comparative degree without "the" is required — "cheaper than", not "the cheaper than". Adding "the" before a comparative followed by "than" is incorrect.

◦ Correct: Ravi said that his red jacket is cheaper than all other jackets.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Ravi said that" and "his red jacket is" are correct.

NOTE

• Comparative + than (cheaper than) takes NO "the"; superlative takes "the" (the cheapest of all). "Cheaper than all other jackets" = "the cheapest jacket".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The author's use of vivid imagery ___________ the reader's senses, making the story come alive.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. heightens.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Heightens" means intensifies / increases / makes stronger. Vivid imagery that makes a story "come alive" clearly heightens (sharpens) the reader's senses. (तीव्र करना / बढ़ाना)

◦ Correct: The author's use of vivid imagery heightens the reader's senses, making the story come alive.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dulls" (weakens) and Option 4 "confuses" contradict "come alive".

• Option 3 "actions" is a noun and is grammatically/semantically wrong here.

NOTE

• Synonyms of heighten: intensify, sharpen, enhance, amplify. Antonyms: dull, diminish, lessen, weaken.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Straight from the horse's mouth
option_1: Hearing something that is untrue or a lie
option_2: Hearing something from a reliable and credible source
option_3: Hearing something that is difficult to understand
option_4: Hearing something coming from a horse's mouth
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Hearing something from a reliable and credible source.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "straight from the horse's mouth" means hearing information directly from the original, most reliable and credible source. (सीधे विश्वसनीय स्रोत से सुनना)

◦ Example: The news of the merger came straight from the horse's mouth — the CEO announced it personally.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (a lie), Option 3 (difficult to understand) and Option 4 (the literal meaning) do not capture the sense of authentic, first-hand information.

NOTE

• The phrase comes from horse racing, where the most reliable tip about a horse would come from the horse itself. Opposite idea: "through the grapevine" (rumour/hearsay).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

He is an intelligent person who always thinks before he ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. acts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main clause is in the simple present ("is", "always thinks") and describes a general habit, so the verb in the "before" clause must also be in the simple present and agree with the singular subject "he" — "acts".

◦ Correct: He is an intelligent person who always thinks before he acts.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "acted" (past) breaks the tense agreement; "acting" (present participle) and "act" (base/plural) do not agree with the singular "he".

NOTE

• With a singular third-person subject (he/she/it) in the simple present, add "-s" to the verb: he acts, she thinks, it works. General truths and habits stay in the present tense.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the realm of literature, words are the (1) ____________ of creation, and authors are the (2) ____________ of meaning. They skillfully weave stories with (3) ____________ narratives that can (4) ____________ the depths of human emotion. A well-crafted novel can (5) ____________ readers into its world, making them forget the passage of time.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. tools.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence says words are the "____ of creation". "Tools" (instruments/means used to make something) fits perfectly — for a writer, words are the tools of creation. (उपकरण / साधन)

◦ Correct: ... words are the tools of creation ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mundane" (dull/ordinary — an adjective) and Option 4 "convey" (a verb) do not fit a noun slot after "the".

• Option 2 "isolate" (to separate) is contextually and grammatically wrong.

NOTE

• The blank needs a plural noun to match "words are the ___". Only "tools" satisfies both the grammar and the meaning.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the realm of literature, words are the (1) ____________ of creation, and authors are the (2) ____________ of meaning. They skillfully weave stories with (3) ____________ narratives that can (4) ____________ the depths of human emotion. A well-crafted novel can (5) ____________ readers into its world, making them forget the passage of time.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. keepers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Authors are described as the "____ of meaning". "Keepers" (guardians/custodians) fits — authors are the keepers (protectors/holders) of meaning. (रक्षक / संरक्षक)

◦ Correct: ... authors are the keepers of meaning ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "direction" (singular, wrong sense), Option 3 "coward" (a timid person) and Option 4 "vibrators" (devices) do not suit "authors are the ___ of meaning".

NOTE

• A "keeper" is one who guards or maintains something (goalkeeper, zookeeper, gatekeeper). Here it conveys authors as custodians who preserve meaning.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the realm of literature, words are the (1) ____________ of creation, and authors are the (2) ____________ of meaning. They skillfully weave stories with (3) ____________ narratives that can (4) ____________ the depths of human emotion. A well-crafted novel can (5) ____________ readers into its world, making them forget the passage of time.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. vivid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank describes the kind of "narratives", so an adjective is needed. "Vivid" means producing powerful, clear, life-like images in the mind. "Vivid narratives" makes the stories come alive. (सजीव / स्पष्ट)

◦ Correct: ... stories with vivid narratives ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "defrost" (a verb — to unfreeze) and Option 4 "convey" (a verb) cannot describe a noun.

• Option 3 "mundane" (dull/ordinary) contradicts the positive, engaging tone of the passage.

NOTE

• Synonyms of vivid: graphic, striking, lively, colourful, life-like. Antonyms: dull, vague, faint, mundane.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the realm of literature, words are the (1) ____________ of creation, and authors are the (2) ____________ of meaning. They skillfully weave stories with (3) ____________ narratives that can (4) ____________ the depths of human emotion. A well-crafted novel can (5) ____________ readers into its world, making them forget the passage of time.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. pilot.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Here "pilot" is used as a verb, meaning to guide, steer or navigate through. Vivid narratives can "pilot the depths of human emotion" — i.e., navigate/steer through them. (मार्गदर्शन करना / नौकायन करना)

◦ Correct: ... narratives that can pilot the depths of human emotion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "teacher", 2 "sailor" and 3 "banker" are nouns (occupations) and cannot function as the verb the blank requires.

NOTE

• "Pilot" can be a noun (one who flies a plane / steers a ship) or a verb (to guide or navigate). As a verb it means to lead or steer something through a course.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the realm of literature, words are the (1) ____________ of creation, and authors are the (2) ____________ of meaning. They skillfully weave stories with (3) ____________ narratives that can (4) ____________ the depths of human emotion. A well-crafted novel can (5) ____________ readers into its world, making them forget the passage of time.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. immerse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Immerse" means to involve someone deeply / absorb them completely. A well-crafted novel can "immerse readers into its world", making them forget time. (डुबो देना / पूरी तरह लीन कर देना)

◦ Correct: A well-crafted novel can immerse readers into its world ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "isolate" (to separate) and Option 4 "repel" (to drive away) are opposite in sense.

• Option 3 "install" (to set up equipment) does not fit readers being drawn into a story.

NOTE

• Synonyms of immerse: absorb, engross, engage, submerge. "Immersed in a book" = deeply engaged in reading it.

question: Which of these state governments has implemented PESA act in November 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Madhya Pradesh government implemented the PESA Act (Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act) in November 2022 (notified the PESA Rules). (मध्य प्रदेश — पेसा अधिनियम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The PESA Act, 1996 extends the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution (Panchayats) to the Fifth Schedule (Scheduled) Areas with certain modifications.

• It empowers Gram Sabhas in tribal areas to manage natural resources, land and local governance and to protect tribal customs and culture.

NOTE

• PESA aims at self-governance for tribal communities. States with Fifth Schedule areas implementing PESA include Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh and Telangana.

question: The national animal of Nepal is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is cow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The national animal of Nepal is the cow (specifically the sacred cow). Nepal is a country where the cow holds great religious and cultural significance. (नेपाल का राष्ट्रीय पशु — गाय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nepal's other national symbols: national bird — Danphe (Himalayan Monal); national flower — Rhododendron (Lali Gurans); national colour — Crimson red.

• Nepal is the only country in the world with a non-rectangular (double-pennant) national flag.

NOTE

• National animals of some neighbours: India — Royal Bengal Tiger; Pakistan — Markhor; Bangladesh — Royal Bengal Tiger; China — Giant Panda; Bhutan — Takin.

question: The cold subarctic climate region possesses forest lands having conifers as main vegetation. These forest lands are known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Taiga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The cold subarctic climate region's coniferous forest lands are known as the "Taiga" (also called boreal forests). They are dominated by evergreen conifers such as pine, spruce and fir. (टैगा / बोरियल वन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Taiga is the world's largest land biome, stretching across northern Russia, Canada and Scandinavia.

• "Mangrove" forests grow in coastal/saline areas; "Savanna" is tropical grassland; "Tundra" is the treeless cold region beyond the taiga.

NOTE

• Major natural vegetation belts (cold to warm): Tundra → Taiga (Boreal) → Temperate deciduous → Mediterranean → Savanna → Tropical rainforest.

question: With reference to medieval history, consider the following statements. 2. One of the important dynasties which ruled in northern India was Gurjara-Pratiharas. 1. The founder of the Chola dynasty called the 'Imperial Cholas' was Vijayalaya (9th century AD). 3. Palas ruled in western India and Rashtrakutas ruled in southern India in the early years (750-1000). Which of the given statement(s) is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement 1 is correct — Vijayalaya (9th century AD) founded the line of the Imperial Cholas by capturing Thanjavur.

• Statement 2 is correct — the Gurjara-Pratiharas were an important dynasty that ruled in northern India.

• Statement 3 is incorrect — the Palas ruled in eastern India (Bengal & Bihar), not western India, and the Rashtrakutas ruled in the Deccan. (So only 1 and 2 are correct.)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Tripartite Struggle for control of Kannauj was fought among the Palas, Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas.

• The Imperial Cholas (Vijayalaya, Rajaraja I, Rajendra I) built a powerful South Indian empire with a strong navy.

NOTE

• Palas — patrons of Buddhism (Vikramshila and Nalanda universities); Pratiharas — known for resisting Arab invasions from the west; Rashtrakutas — built the Kailasa temple at Ellora.

question: Which of the following statements is/are true for the Religious Festivals in India? 1. Losar festival is majorly celebrated by Buddhist community of India. 2. Navroz festival is majorly celebrated by the Parsi community of India. 3. Saga Dawa is majorly celebrated by the Muslim community of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement 1 is correct — Losar (the Tibetan New Year) is celebrated mainly by the Buddhist community (in Ladakh, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, etc.).

• Statement 2 is correct — Navroz (Nowruz), the Parsi New Year, is celebrated mainly by the Parsi (Zoroastrian) community of India.

• Statement 3 is incorrect — Saga Dawa is a Buddhist festival (celebrated in Sikkim, marking Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death), NOT a Muslim festival.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Losar falls in February–March; Saga Dawa falls on the full-moon day of the fourth Tibetan month.

• Navroz marks the beginning of the Iranian/Zoroastrian New Year and the spring equinox.

NOTE

• Buddhist festivals: Losar, Saga Dawa, Buddha Purnima, Hemis. Parsi festival: Navroz. Knowing the community–festival match is a common SSC GK question.

question: Birju Maharaj is related to which of the following classical dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Birju Maharaj was the legendary exponent of the Kathak classical dance form. He belonged to the Lucknow (Kalka-Bindadin) Gharana of Kathak. (कथक — बिरजू महाराज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh), characterised by fast footwork (tatkar), spins (chakkars) and expressive storytelling.

• Birju Maharaj was awarded the Padma Vibhushan and also choreographed dances for films such as *Devdas* and *Bajirao Mastani*.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which of the following peaks is NOT located in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dhaulagiri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dhaulagiri is located in Nepal, NOT in India. It is one of the world's highest peaks (about 8,167 m), the seventh-highest in the world. (धौलागिरि — नेपाल में)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Guru Shikhar is the highest peak of the Aravalli Range (in Rajasthan/Mount Abu).

• Nanda Devi (Uttarakhand) is the highest peak entirely within India.

• Mahendragiri is a peak in the Eastern Ghats (Odisha).

NOTE

• Highest peak in India — Kangchenjunga (Sikkim). Highest in the world — Mount Everest (Nepal). Both Everest and Dhaulagiri lie in Nepal.

question: In which year did John Dalton present his atomic theory, the second part of which states that all atoms of a particular element are equal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1808.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• John Dalton presented his atomic theory in 1808. One of its postulates states that all atoms of a given element are identical (equal) in mass and properties. (डाल्टन का परमाणु सिद्धांत — 1808)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Key postulates of Dalton's Atomic Theory (1808): matter is made of tiny indivisible atoms; atoms of the same element are identical; atoms of different elements differ; atoms combine in fixed whole-number ratios to form compounds; atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

NOTE

• Dalton's theory laid the foundation of modern chemistry. Later discoveries (electron, proton, neutron, isotopes) modified the idea that atoms are indivisible and that all atoms of an element are identical.

question: Padma Bhushan awardee Mogubai Kurdikar was associated with which of the following music styles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindustani Classical music.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mogubai Kurdikar, a Padma Bhushan awardee, was a celebrated exponent of Hindustani Classical music. She belonged to the Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana. (हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय संगीत — मोगुबाई कुर्दीकर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• She was the mother and guru of the legendary vocalist Kishori Amonkar.

• The Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana was founded by Ustad Alladiya Khan.

NOTE

• Hindustani (North Indian) classical music is based on ragas and talas; its two main styles of vocal music are Dhrupad and Khayal. It differs from Carnatic (South Indian) classical music.

question: Who among the following elect(s) the presiding officer of the Vidhan Sabha in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Members of Vidhan Sabha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The presiding officer of the Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly) — the Speaker — is elected by the Members of the Vidhan Sabha (MLAs) from among themselves. (विधान सभा के अध्यक्ष का चुनाव विधायकों द्वारा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Speaker presides over the Assembly, maintains order and decides on points of order; the Deputy Speaker acts in the Speaker's absence.

• Both are elected by the members of the Assembly and can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of the members.

NOTE

• Article 178 provides for the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly. Similarly, the Lok Sabha elects its Speaker, and the Vidhan Parishad has a Chairman.

question: Who is the author of the historical fiction novel 'The Mauryan: The Legend of Ashoka'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Komal Bhanver.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The historical fiction novel "The Mauryan: The Legend of Ashoka" was written by Komal Bhanver. (लेखिका — कोमल भानवर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The novel is set in the era of the Mauryan Empire and revolves around the life and legend of Emperor Ashoka.

• The Mauryan Empire (321–185 BCE) was founded by Chandragupta Maurya with the guidance of Chanakya (Kautilya).

NOTE

• Other popular authors: Amish Tripathi (Shiva Trilogy, Ram Chandra Series), Chetan Bhagat (Five Point Someone, Half Girlfriend), Sanjeev Sanyal (The Ocean of Churn, Land of the Seven Rivers).

question: Which of the following is an informal group consisting of 4 to 10 individuals who seek loans against mutual guarantee?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Joint liability group.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Joint Liability Group (JLG)" is an informal group of usually 4 to 10 individuals who come together to avail bank loans against a mutual guarantee, typically for agricultural and allied activities. (संयुक्त देयता समूह — पारस्परिक गारंटी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In a JLG, members are jointly and severally liable for repayment — if one defaults, others are responsible.

• A Self-Help Group (SHG) is usually a larger group (10–20 members) that pools savings, whereas a JLG focuses on group-guaranteed credit.

NOTE

• The JLG concept was promoted by NABARD to extend credit to small/marginal farmers and tenant farmers who lack collateral.

question: Who has been appointed as the new Chief of the Special Protection Group (SPG) by the centre in November 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alok Sharma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alok Sharma was appointed as the new Director (Chief) of the Special Protection Group (SPG) by the Centre in November 2023. (एसपीजी प्रमुख — आलोक शर्मा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Special Protection Group (SPG) was constituted in 1988 and is responsible for the security of the Prime Minister of India.

• The SPG functions under the Cabinet Secretariat and its personnel are drawn mainly from central police organisations.

NOTE

• After the 2019 amendment, the SPG provides security only to the incumbent Prime Minister and their immediate family members residing with them at the official residence.

question: Which state in India hosted the 77th edition of the Santosh Trophy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arunachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 77th edition of the Santosh Trophy (2023–24) was hosted by Arunachal Pradesh. (संतोष ट्रॉफी — अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Santosh Trophy is a premier football knock-out competition contested by the states and government institutions of India, organised by the All India Football Federation (AIFF) since 1941.

• Services football team is the most successful side in Santosh Trophy history.

NOTE

• The trophy is named after Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhary of Santosh (now in Bangladesh). West Bengal is among the most successful states in this tournament.

question: Which of the following vitamins includes cobalt as an essential component?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vitamin B12.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) contains cobalt as an essential central component of its molecule — that is why it is called "cobalamin". (विटामिन B12 — कोबाल्ट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Vitamin B12 is essential for the formation of red blood cells and the proper functioning of the nervous system; its deficiency causes pernicious anaemia.

• It is found mainly in animal products (meat, eggs, milk, fish); vegetarians may need supplements.

NOTE

• Chemical names of vitamins: A — Retinol; B1 — Thiamine; C — Ascorbic acid; D — Calciferol; E — Tocopherol; K — Phylloquinone; B12 — Cobalamin.

question: Who among the following was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Annie Besant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Annie Besant became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress in 1917 (Calcutta session). (कांग्रेस की पहली महिला अध्यक्ष — एनी बेसेंट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Annie Besant was an Irish-origin theosophist and social reformer who founded the Home Rule League (1916) and the newspaper New India.

• Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President of the Congress (1925, Kanpur session) and the first woman Governor of an Indian state (UP).

NOTE

• The first President of the INC was W. C. Bonnerjee (1885, Bombay). Sucheta Kripalani was India's first woman Chief Minister (Uttar Pradesh).

question: ________ was awarded, Padma Shri in 1970 for his contribution to the field of Kuchipudi dance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is V Satyanarayana Sarma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma was awarded the Padma Shri in 1970 for his contribution to the Kuchipudi dance form. He was renowned for his portrayal of female roles, especially Satyabhama in *Bhama Kalapam*. (कुचिपुड़ी — वी. सत्यनारायण शर्मा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance-drama form of Andhra Pradesh, combining dance, music and dramatic performance.

• It takes its name from the village Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh and was systematised by Siddhendra Yogi.

NOTE

• The eight recognised classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: The construction of Mehrangarh fort of Jodhpur was initiated during the reign of which ruler?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rao Jodha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The construction of the Mehrangarh Fort of Jodhpur (Rajasthan) was initiated in 1459 by Rao Jodha, the Rathore ruler and founder of Jodhpur. (मेहरानगढ़ किला — राव जोधा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Mehrangarh Fort stands on a hill about 125 m above the city and is one of the largest forts in India, known for its imposing walls, palaces (Moti Mahal, Phool Mahal) and a rich museum.

• Jodhpur is called the "Blue City" and the "Sun City".

NOTE

• Rao Jodha founded the city of Jodhpur in 1459. Rao Bika (his son) founded Bikaner. Both belonged to the Rathore dynasty of Marwar.

question: The major carbohydrate of milk is
solution_text:
The correct answer is lactose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The major carbohydrate present in milk is "lactose", a disaccharide made of glucose + galactose. It is also called "milk sugar". (दुग्ध शर्करा — लैक्टोज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• People who cannot digest lactose (due to a deficiency of the enzyme lactase) suffer from lactose intolerance.

• Other disaccharides: Sucrose (glucose + fructose, table sugar), Maltose (glucose + glucose, malt sugar).

NOTE

• Fructose is fruit sugar; starch is a storage polysaccharide in plants; glucose is the primary energy source in the body. Milk's characteristic sugar is lactose.

question: Who became the Nawab of Bengal after the death of Alivardi Khan in the year 1756?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Siraj-Ud-Daulah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Siraj-ud-Daulah became the Nawab of Bengal in 1756 after the death of his grandfather Alivardi Khan. (बंगाल का नवाब — सिराजुद्दौला, 1756)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Siraj-ud-Daulah captured the British Fort William in Calcutta, an event linked to the alleged "Black Hole of Calcutta".

• He was defeated by Robert Clive at the Battle of Plassey (1757) due to the betrayal of his commander Mir Jafar, marking the beginning of British political control in India.

NOTE

• After Plassey, Mir Jafar became the puppet Nawab. The Battle of Buxar (1764) further consolidated British power, leading to the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha (1765).

question: Which of the following iron and steel plants is located in Jharkhand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bokaro.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bokaro Steel Plant is located in Bokaro, Jharkhand. It was set up with the assistance of the erstwhile Soviet Union (USSR) and is run by the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL). (बोकारो इस्पात संयंत्र — झारखंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Durgapur steel plant is in West Bengal; Salem steel plant is in Tamil Nadu; Vijayanagar (JSW) steel plant is in Karnataka.

• Other SAIL plants: Bhilai (Chhattisgarh), Rourkela (Odisha), Durgapur & Burnpur/IISCO (West Bengal).

NOTE

• Jharkhand is also home to the Tata Steel plant at Jamshedpur (TISCO), India's first major private-sector iron and steel plant (1907).

question: What is a 'double fault' in tennis?
option_1: Serving two faults in a row
option_2: A serve that goes out of bounds
option_3: A fault called by the linesman
option_4: A serve that hits the net and goes into the correct service box
solution_text:
The correct answer is Serving two faults in a row.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In tennis, a "double fault" occurs when the server fails both the first and the second serve (two faults in a row), resulting in the loss of that point to the opponent. (डबल फॉल्ट — लगातार दो गलत सर्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Each server gets two chances to serve; missing both is a double fault.

• A serve that hits the net but lands in the correct service box is a "let" (the serve is replayed), not a fault.

NOTE

• Tennis terms: Ace (an unreturnable serve), Fault (a bad serve), Deuce (40–40), Love (zero), Break point, Grand Slam (winning all four majors).

question: The 11th Fundamental Duty to the Indian Constitution was added in the year ____________ by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2002.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 11th Fundamental Duty was added to the Constitution in 2002 by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. (11वां मौलिक कर्तव्य — 2002, 86वां संशोधन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The 11th Fundamental Duty [Article 51A(k)] makes it a duty of every parent/guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child/ward between the ages of 6 and 14 years.

• The 86th Amendment also inserted Article 21A (Right to Education as a fundamental right).

NOTE

• The original 10 Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IV-A, Article 51A.

question: Which of the following Census recorded negative population growth in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1921.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Census of 1921 recorded a negative population growth in India. The year 1921 is therefore known as the "Great Divide / Year of Great Divide" in India's demographic history. (1921 — नकारात्मक जनसंख्या वृद्धि)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The population decline in 1921 was due to widespread famines, epidemics (especially the influenza/Spanish flu pandemic of 1918–19), and poor health conditions.

• After 1921, India's population has grown continuously (the phase of steady/rapid growth).

NOTE

• 1921 = Year of the Great Divide (population fell). 1951 = beginning of the population explosion. The Census in India is conducted every 10 years; the first synchronous census was in 1881.

question: Kharavela was an important ruler of which dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chedi Dynasty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kharavela was the greatest ruler of the Chedi (Mahameghavahana) dynasty of Kalinga (present-day Odisha). (खारवेल — चेदि/महामेघवाहन वंश, कलिंग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Information about Kharavela comes mainly from the Hathigumpha Inscription (in the Udayagiri caves near Bhubaneswar), written in Prakrit using the Brahmi script.

• He was a follower and great patron of Jainism.

NOTE

• The Hathigumpha inscription describes Kharavela's military conquests and public works. The Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves were built for Jain monks during his reign.
